notes: Type markers from Adobe AMF 3. The original Adobe wiki PDF is no longer online; this file is that specification. Values are original (kelp, harbor, 7, 1.5).

cases.title: Null
cases.paragraph: The null marker is 0x01. No further bytes follow.

cases.title: Integer 7
cases.paragraph: The integer marker is 0x04. The value is a U29. Integers 0 through 127 are one byte. 7 is 0x07.

cases.title: Double 1.5
cases.paragraph: The double marker is 0x05. The next eight bytes are an IEEE-754 double in network byte order. 1.5 is 0x3ff8000000000000.

cases.title: String kelp
cases.paragraph: The string marker is 0x06. A U29 with the low bit set carries the length in the remaining bits, then that many UTF-8 bytes. kelp has length 4, so the U29 is 0x09.

cases.title: Empty string
cases.paragraph: An empty string is marker 0x06 and U29 0x01 (length 0, low bit set).

cases.title: Dense array [1, 2]
cases.paragraph: The array marker is 0x09. A U29 dense count (low bit set) is followed by an empty associative part (the empty string) and then the dense values. 1 and 2 are U29 integers.

cases.title: Dynamic object n = 7
cases.paragraph: The object marker is 0x0A. Traits U29 0x0B is a new dynamic anonymous trait with no sealed members. The class name is the empty string. Dynamic members follow until an empty name.

cases.title: Dynamic object harbor = kelp
cases.paragraph: A dynamic string member is a U29 string name, then a string value. An empty name ends the dynamic members.

cases.title: Empty buffer
cases.paragraph: A value begins with a type marker. An empty buffer is not a value.

cases.title: Integer marker without a U29
cases.paragraph: An integer is the marker plus a U29. The marker alone is not an integer.

cases.title: Array count without values
cases.paragraph: A dense count of 2 requires two values after the associative part. The count and the empty associative name alone are not an array.

cases.title: Marker 0xFF
cases.paragraph: 0xFF is not an AMF3 type marker.
